Enquiry & qualificationStandard3–5 weeks

Marketplace and website enquiry capture with routing

Pull every enquiry from IndiaMART, TradeIndia, the website and the RFQ inbox into one CRM queue, remove duplicates, extract what the buyer needs and route it to the right product or territory owner with a response deadline.

Industrial & engineering manufacturers · Process, chemical & pharma manufacturing · Contract & private-label manufacturing

Open the automation blueprint

The problem

Enquiries arrive through marketplace dashboards, email, website forms, phone calls and trade-fair cards. Sales coordinators copy them by hand, duplicates from the same buyer go to two reps, and enquiries that arrive after hours wait until someone notices them. Buyers who send the same RFQ to several suppliers often shortlist whoever replies first with a sensible question.

Trigger

A new lead appears through the IndiaMART Lead Manager API, a marketplace or website form notification arrives, or an email lands in the shared RFQ inbox.

How it runs

  • Collect leads from the IndiaMART Lead Manager API, other marketplace notifications, website forms and the RFQ mailbox into one queue.
  • Normalize names, phone numbers, company names and GSTIN where given, then match against existing CRM accounts and open enquiries to avoid duplicate follow-up.
  • Use an AI model to extract product, grade or specification, quantity, delivery location, required date and attachments, and list missing information as questions for the rep.
  • Score fit against agreed rules such as product range, minimum order, serviceable region and buyer type, and route to the product or territory owner with a response deadline.
  • Send an acknowledgement by email, or by WhatsApp only where the buyer started the chat or opted in, and alert the owner in Slack or the CRM app.
  • Escalate enquiries with no human response by the deadline to the sales coordinator.

Human checkpoint

The sales coordinator reviews low-confidence extractions, out-of-territory enquiries and anything flagged as a large or strategic account before routing. Reps qualify every enquiry by call or email; the automation never sends prices or delivery commitments.

Specification, samples & quoteAdvanced6–10 weeks

RFQ-to-quote drafting with estimator approval

Turn RFQ emails, drawings and BOQs into a structured costing draft based on your item master, past quotes and current rates, so the estimator reviews and approves a quote instead of building it from scratch, and the eventual PO is checked against it.

Industrial & engineering manufacturers · Contract & private-label manufacturing

Open the automation blueprint

The problem

Quoting depends on one or two experienced estimators who rebuild costing sheets in Excel for every RFQ, look up old quotes from memory and chase purchase for current material rates. Turnaround slips when they are on the shop floor or traveling, assumptions are not recorded, and the same part can be priced differently for different buyers.

Trigger

An enquiry is marked qualified in the CRM with an RFQ, drawing, specification sheet, formulation brief or BOQ attached.

How it runs

  • Extract line items, material grade, quantity breaks, finish, packing and delivery terms from the RFQ, BOQ and drawing title blocks and notes, flagging any dimension or tolerance it cannot read with confidence.
  • Match each line to the item master, released drawing revisions where the PDM exposes an API or export, and similar past quotes, and show what changed since the last quote to this buyer.
  • Pull current raw material rates, machine-hour or conversion rates, tooling and freight assumptions from the rate tables maintained by purchase and costing.
  • Generate a costing sheet and quote draft in the standard template, with assumptions, deviations from the buyer's specification and open technical questions listed.
  • Route the draft to the estimator in a review screen; discounts beyond the agreed matrix go to the sales head for approval.
  • Send the approved quote as a PDF from the rep's address, log the version in the CRM, schedule follow-ups and capture win or loss reasons at close.
  • When the buyer's PO arrives, compare price, quantity, delivery and terms with the approved quote and stage a draft sales order for the commercial manager.

Human checkpoint

The estimator or applications engineer checks every technical interpretation, cost element and price before release, and the sales head approves discounts outside the matrix. Nothing reaches a buyer without a named approver recorded against that quote version.

Margin fields are hidden from roles that do not need them, and files follow the client's document retention policy.

Order & credit checkStandard4–6 weeks

Dealer and distributor ordering on WhatsApp or a portal

Let registered dealers place orders on WhatsApp or a simple portal, validated against the ERP price list, schemes, pack sizes, stock and credit position before a draft sales order reaches the order desk.

Distributors & dealer networks

Open the automation blueprint

The problem

Dealers send orders as WhatsApp texts, photos of handwritten lists and calls to the sales rep. The order desk re-types them into Tally or the ERP, confirms stock and schemes by phone and discovers credit holds only after the order is entered. Orders get missed in the month-end rush, SKU codes are misread, and dealers have no confirmation of what was actually booked.

Trigger

A dealer whose WhatsApp number is mapped to a customer code sends an order message or completes a WhatsApp Flow, or submits a cart on the dealer portal.

How it runs

  • Identify the dealer from the registered number or portal login and load their price list, schemes and usual SKUs from the ERP or Tally through its API or a scheduled sync.
  • Read the order from the WhatsApp Flow, portal cart or free text, map items to SKU codes and pack sizes, and ask the dealer to confirm any line the system is unsure about.
  • Check stock or available-to-promise by warehouse, minimum order and scheme eligibility, and show partial availability or approved substitutes.
  • Check the dealer's credit limit and overdue balance from the receivables feed and flag the order for hold if limits are crossed.
  • Create a draft sales order in the ERP or order queue for the order desk, and send an approved confirmation template with the order reference once it is released.

Human checkpoint

The order desk releases every order with an exception: unclear SKUs, price or scheme overrides, stock shortfalls or credit flags. Orders on credit hold are released only by the credit controller. Prices and schemes always come from the ERP, never from the AI.

Payment & collectionsStandard3–5 weeks

Credit-limit checks and overdue payment reminders

Compute each dealer's exposure against their credit limit every day, flag orders for hold, and send courteous ledger-based reminders before and after due dates, with escalation to the rep and then the credit controller.

Distributors & dealer networks

Open the automation blueprint

The problem

Receivables live in Tally or the ERP, but credit decisions happen in conversations. Reps keep booking orders for dealers who are over their limit, reminders depend on whoever has time, and disputes about schemes, credit notes or short supply surface only when a payment is already late. Month-end becomes a round of phone calls.

Trigger

A nightly receivables and aging export from the ERP, a new order from a dealer, or an invoice reaching an agreed reminder point before or after its due date.

How it runs

  • Pull outstanding invoices, credit notes, receipts and aging per dealer from Tally or the ERP and reconcile totals with the accounts team's ledger.
  • Calculate exposure against the approved credit limit and payment terms, and mark each dealer as clear, watch or hold.
  • Send approved WhatsApp utility templates or emails about the dealer's own account, with a ledger statement, to the nominated accounts contact at agreed points around the due date.
  • Capture replies such as payment made, promise to pay or dispute, and route disputes about schemes, credit notes or short supply to the right owner.
  • Escalate unresolved overdues to the rep, then to the credit controller, and send finance a weekly collections summary.

Human checkpoint

The credit controller decides credit limits, holds, releases, extensions and any legal step. Reminders use approved, non-threatening wording, and an open dispute pauses reminders for that invoice until a person resolves it.

Invoice, dispatch & deliverStandard3–5 weeks

Dispatch updates with invoice, e-way bill and documents

When an order is invoiced and dispatched, send the buyer the invoice, e-way bill number, transporter and vehicle details, plus the CoA and safety data sheet where needed, and alert the dispatch team before an e-way bill expires in transit.

Distributors & dealer networks · Process, chemical & pharma manufacturing

Open the automation blueprint

The problem

Buyers and dealers call the sales rep to ask whether goods have left, which transporter is carrying them and when they will arrive. Dispatch teams forward invoice photos on WhatsApp, certificates of analysis are emailed separately, and e-way bills sometimes lapse on delayed consignments because nobody is watching validity.

Trigger

The ERP marks an invoice as posted with an IRN and e-way bill number, or the transporter updates the lorry receipt or vehicle number.

How it runs

  • Read invoice number, IRN status, e-way bill number and validity, transporter, vehicle number and LR details from the ERP or GSP integration.
  • Check for gaps such as missing Part B vehicle details, values that differ between invoice and e-way bill, or missing batch documents, and alert dispatch before the truck leaves.
  • Attach the invoice and, for chemical and pharma shipments, the batch certificate of analysis released by QC and, for hazardous products, the current safety data sheet from the regulatory or EHS owner.
  • Send an approved dispatch template to the buyer's opted-in contacts with document links and the expected delivery window.
  • Watch e-way bill validity against transit status, alert the dispatch lead and transporter before the extension window opens, and capture proof of delivery from the transporter.

Human checkpoint

The dispatch lead handles every exception; vehicle changes and e-way bill extensions are made in the e-way bill system by the dispatch team or the transporter carrying the goods. The automation never generates, cancels or extends e-invoices or e-way bills; it reads status and alerts people. Only QC releases CoAs.

Service, field visits & reorderStandard4–6 weeks

Sales rep beat planning and visit reporting

Plan weekly dealer and retailer beats from sales, overdue and stock data, then let reps report each visit as a short WhatsApp voice note or form that becomes a structured CRM record and a daily summary for managers.

Distributors & dealer networks

Open the automation blueprint

The problem

Field reps plan visits from memory, return to the same easy dealers and report the day as a long WhatsApp message to their manager. Competitor activity, display issues, stock gaps and complaints stay in chats instead of the CRM, so head office cannot see coverage or follow up on what dealers asked for.

Trigger

A weekly planning run on Monday morning, and each visit check-in or voice note a rep sends from the field.

How it runs

  • Suggest a weekly beat per rep from dealer sales trends, overdue status, last visit date and open complaints, for the area manager to adjust and approve.
  • Let the rep check in at a visit and send a voice note or short form on WhatsApp or the CRM app.
  • Transcribe the note and extract order intent, stock gaps, competitor activity, complaints and promised actions into structured fields for the rep to confirm.
  • Create follow-up tasks for orders, service requests or scheme queries and assign them to the right team.
  • Send managers a daily coverage summary and a weekly view of planned versus completed visits.

Human checkpoint

Area managers approve beat plans and review exceptions. Reps confirm each extracted visit record before it is saved. The system reports planned and completed visits only; any decision about a rep's performance rests with their manager, using fuller context.

Service, field visits & reorderAdvanced6–8 weeks

Service, AMC and warranty tickets with spare-part requests

Log service requests with machine serial number, photos and symptoms, check warranty or AMC status, assign the right engineer, suggest checks from approved manuals and turn spare-part needs into stock checks or quotes.

Industrial & engineering manufacturers · Distributors & dealer networks

Open the automation blueprint

The problem

Customers and dealers report breakdowns by calling whoever they know. Service coordinators look up warranty and AMC status in spreadsheets, engineers travel without the right spare or manual, and parts quotes for out-of-warranty machines take days. AMC renewals lapse because nobody tracks expiry dates.

Trigger

A customer or dealer raises a request on WhatsApp, the portal or by email, or an AMC visit or renewal date comes due.

How it runs

  • Capture the machine serial number, site, symptoms, error codes and photos through a guided WhatsApp or portal form.
  • Check the serial number against the installed base, warranty terms and AMC contract, and show the machine's service history.
  • Suggest likely causes and checks for the engineer from approved manuals and past tickets, with links to the source pages.
  • Assign an engineer by territory, skill and availability, start SLA timers and update the customer with approved templates.
  • For parts, check stock and raise a warranty replacement request or an out-of-warranty quote for approval; remind customers of AMC renewals and preventive visits.
  • Close the ticket with the engineer's report, parts used and customer sign-off.

Human checkpoint

The service engineer diagnoses and decides the repair, and the service manager approves warranty acceptance or rejection and any goodwill. Faults involving guarding, interlocks, pressure or electrical hazards go straight to an engineer; the assistant never advises bypassing a safety device.

Plan, procure, make & checkStandard4–6 weeks

Daily production and OEE-style reporting from ERP and MES data

Collect shift production, downtime and rejection entries from the ERP, MES or shift sheets, check them for gaps, and publish a plant dashboard and a short written summary in time for the morning production meeting.

Industrial & engineering manufacturers · Process, chemical & pharma manufacturing

Open the automation blueprint

The problem

Production figures arrive from different lines as Excel sheets, WhatsApp photos of logbooks and ERP entries made a day late. The morning meeting spends its time agreeing numbers instead of acting on them, downtime reasons are recorded inconsistently, and lines or shifts cannot be compared reliably.

Trigger

A scheduled run after each shift or at a fixed time before the morning meeting, reading the latest ERP, MES or shift sheet data.

How it runs

  • Pull shift output, planned and actual run time, downtime with reason codes, rejections and rework from ERP, MES exports or structured shift sheets.
  • Flag missing shifts, impossible values and unmapped downtime reasons to the line supervisor before the report runs.
  • Model the data in a warehouse with agreed definitions and calculate availability, performance and quality where machine and standard-rate data allow; for batch plants, report yield and cycle time per batch.
  • Publish a Power BI dashboard by plant, line, shift and product, with trends and the top downtime reasons.
  • Draft a short written summary of the main variances for the plant head, linked to the underlying numbers.

Human checkpoint

Line supervisors confirm reason codes and corrections before figures are published, and the plant head reviews the written summary and owns any action. For GxP plants the dashboard is a reporting copy; batch records in validated systems remain the record.

Plan, procure, make & checkStandard4–6 weeks

Quality NCR, customer complaint and CAPA routing

Raise non-conformances and customer complaints with photos, lot and part details, route them to the right quality owner, track containment and CAPA actions to closure, and draft 8D reports for QA approval.

Industrial & engineering manufacturers · Contract & private-label manufacturing

Open the automation blueprint

The problem

NCRs are raised on paper or by email, containment depends on who remembers, and CAPA due dates slip between shifts. OEM customers and brand owners expect 8D reports and evidence of effectiveness checks, but the quality team spends days compiling them from scattered photos, test results and email threads.

Trigger

An inspector logs a non-conformance at incoming, in-process or final inspection, or a customer complaint arrives by email, portal or through the account manager.

How it runs

  • Capture the NCR with part or product, drawing revision, batch or lot, quantity, defect type and photos through a mobile form.
  • Assign a number, route it to the QA owner for that product line and open containment tasks with due dates.
  • Show similar past NCRs and their root causes, and draft a structured 5-why or 8D outline from the record for the quality engineer to complete.
  • Track corrective and preventive actions, send reminders before due dates and schedule effectiveness checks.
  • Compile the customer-facing 8D or complaint response from approved content for QA sign-off.

Human checkpoint

The QA manager decides disposition (use as is, rework, scrap or return) and approves root cause, CAPA closure and every customer-facing report. AI output is marked as draft and never closes a record. On GxP sites, deviations and CAPAs stay in the validated QMS.

Plan, procure, make & checkStandard4–6 weeks

Preventive maintenance alerts and breakdown logging

Generate maintenance work orders from calendar, run-hour or count schedules, remind technicians and supervisors before due dates, log breakdowns with cause and spares used, and track statutory inspection dates.

Industrial & engineering manufacturers · Process, chemical & pharma manufacturing

Open the automation blueprint

The problem

Preventive maintenance schedules sit in Excel or in a CMMS nobody updates. Tasks are skipped under production pressure, breakdowns are fixed without recording cause or parts, and due dates for statutory inspections of lifting equipment and pressure vessels live in one person's diary.

Trigger

A schedule threshold is reached by date, run hours or production count from MES or meter readings, or an operator reports a breakdown.

How it runs

  • Set up the asset register with maintenance plans, checklists and statutory inspection due dates agreed with the maintenance head.
  • Create work orders ahead of the due date and notify the assigned technician and supervisor, escalating tasks that become overdue.
  • Let technicians close work orders on mobile with checklist results, readings, photos and spares used.
  • Log breakdowns with symptom, cause, downtime and parts, and feed them into MTBF and MTTR reporting.
  • Remind the safety officer and the occupier's team of upcoming statutory inspections and the reports due from competent persons.

Human checkpoint

The maintenance head approves schedule changes and every deferral, and safety-critical tasks cannot be deferred without a named sign-off. For GxP equipment, calibration and maintenance records stay in the validated CMMS or logbook; this workflow only sends reminders.

Plan, procure, make & checkStarter2–4 weeks

Supplier PO follow-ups and inbound material tracking

Follow up open purchase orders before their due dates, read supplier replies into expected dates for the buyer to confirm, and flag shortages against the production plan or dealer backorders.

Distributors & dealer networks · Contract & private-label manufacturing

Open the automation blueprint

The problem

Buyers chase suppliers and principals by phone and email for every open PO. Revised dates stay in inboxes, planning learns about a packaging or raw material shortage on the day of production, and distributors discover a principal's short supply only when dealers complain.

Trigger

An open PO line approaches its due date, a supplier replies to a follow-up, or a goods receipt differs from the PO.

How it runs

  • Read open PO lines, due dates and supplier contacts from the ERP every morning.
  • Send templated follow-up emails before and on the due date from the buyer's mailbox or a shared purchase address.
  • Use AI to read supplier replies for committed dates, partial quantities and issues, and propose updated expected dates for the buyer to confirm.
  • Compare expected receipts with the production plan or dealer backorders and flag shortages to planning or sales.
  • Flag goods receipt mismatches, and alert accounts as invoices from registered micro or small suppliers near the MSMED Act payment deadline, which cannot exceed 45 days from acceptance.

Human checkpoint

The buyer confirms every revised date before it reaches planning. Changes to PO price, quantity or supplier are made only by the purchase manager in the ERP. Shortfalls of client-supplied material are raised with the brand client by the account manager.

Invoice, dispatch & deliverStandard4–6 weeks

Export documentation checklist for chemical and pharma shipments

For each export order, build the document checklist by destination, incoterm and product, prefill drafts from ERP data, check consistency across documents and track every item through to the shipping bill and bill of lading.

Process, chemical & pharma manufacturing

Open the automation blueprint

The problem

Chemical and pharma exports need a long, product-specific set of documents: commercial invoice, packing list, certificate of origin, certificates of analysis, safety data sheets, dangerous goods declarations and buyer-specific regulatory papers. Errors in HS codes, quantities or consignee details cause port delays and payment disputes, and status lives in email threads with the CHA.

Trigger

An export sales order is confirmed in the ERP, or a booking confirmation arrives from the freight forwarder.

How it runs

  • Generate a checklist from rules for the destination, incoterm, product class and buyer requirements, with an owner and due date for each document.
  • Prefill the commercial invoice and packing list from the ERP, and attach the batch CoA, safety data sheet and LUT reference for exports made without payment of IGST.
  • Check HS code, quantities, weights, values, batch numbers and consignee details for consistency across all documents and highlight mismatches.
  • Share the draft set with the CHA and freight forwarder, and track shipping bill, certificate of origin and bill of lading status.
  • Remind finance to track export realization once the shipping bill and bill of lading are received.

Human checkpoint

The export documentation executive verifies every document before release. HS and dangerous goods classification and regulatory documents are decided by the trade compliance or regulatory owner, and the CHA files the shipping bill. The automation never submits a filing.

Specification, samples & quoteStandard5–7 weeks

Private-label sample, artwork and approval tracking

Track each brand client's brief, samples, feedback rounds, artwork and label approvals and first-order readiness in one shared portal, so both sides can see what is pending and who must act next.

Contract & private-label manufacturing

Open the automation blueprint

The problem

Contract manufacturers run many brand projects at once. Briefs arrive on WhatsApp, sample versions are tracked in a spreadsheet, feedback is scattered across calls and chats, and artwork goes through several rounds before anyone checks the mandatory label declarations. Projects stall because nobody knows whether the client or the factory owes the next step.

Trigger

A new brand client brief is accepted, a sample is dispatched, client feedback arrives, or an artwork version is uploaded.

How it runs

  • Capture the brief in a structured form: product type, specification or formulation targets, pack format, MOQ, target cost and timeline.
  • Create a project with stages for samples, feedback, stability or testing, artwork, label approval and first order, each with an owner and due date.
  • Log each sample version with its R&D or QA release, courier tracking and client feedback, keeping a full version history.
  • Run each artwork version through a mandatory-declarations checklist for the product category before the client sees it, and record the client's named approver and approval date.
  • Notify the next owner when a stage completes, send weekly status to the client contact, and convert approved projects into a sales order and BOM request.

Human checkpoint

R&D or QA releases each sample. The manufacturer's regulatory or QA owner confirms label declarations for the product category, such as Legal Metrology, FSSAI, cosmetics or drug labeling rules. The brand client's named approver signs off artwork in the portal before printing.

Brand clients' confidential formulations, specifications and artwork. Each client sees only their own projects. Files are stored with access logging and kept as the contract and quality record requirements specify. WhatsApp updates go only to client contacts who opted in.

  • Sample version and feedback history
  • Artwork declarations checklist and approval log

  • Feedback rounds per project
  • Artwork rounds before approval

Plan, procure, make & checkAdvanced5–8 weeks

Batch release readiness tracker around validated systems

Show, for every batch, whether production records, QC tests, deviations and documents are complete by reading status from validated systems, and remind the right reviewers, without touching the GxP record itself.

Process, chemical & pharma manufacturing · Contract & private-label manufacturing

Open the automation blueprint

The problem

Finished batches wait in quarantine while QA chases missing signatures, pending QC tests, open deviations and CoA drafts across separate systems and paper records. Planning and sales cannot tell when stock will be released, so they call QA repeatedly, and brand clients ask for status the plant cannot easily give.

Trigger

A batch is completed in the ERP or MES, or the status of a QC test, deviation or batch record review changes in its source system.

How it runs

  • Read batch status, QC test status from the LIMS, open deviations from the QMS and batch record review status through read-only exports or reports.
  • Show a readiness board per batch listing what is complete, what is pending and the responsible reviewer.
  • Send reminders to reviewers for overdue items and a daily summary of batches expected to be ready for the release decision.
  • Give planning, sales and brand clients a release-expected view without exposing GxP record content.

Human checkpoint

Only QA releases or rejects a batch, following site SOPs in the validated systems. The tracker is a read-only, non-GxP reporting layer introduced through the site's change control, and it never creates, edits or approves a GxP record or signature.

Tools

PPythonSSupabaseRRetoolnn8nSSlack

Systems it connects

  • LIMS such as LabWare or STARLIMS
  • QMS for deviations and CAPA
  • ERP or MES batch records
  • Batch record review log

Data & consent

Batch and test status data only. The tracker copies just the status fields needed for reminders, with timestamps and source references, and refreshes rather than edits them. Access is role-based, brand clients see only their own batches, and retention follows the site's document control policy.

What we deliver

  • Read-only status integration with LIMS, QMS and ERP
  • Batch readiness board
  • Reviewer reminders and daily summary
  • Release-expected view for planning and clients

How we measure it

  • Batch completion to release time
  • Batches waiting on a single pending item
  • Overdue review items
  • Release date queries to QA
